title: fix(renderer): erase through rows a narrowing terminal rewrapped
body:
Fixes #1867.

Before the resize erase, move the cursor up past the extra terminal rows the narrowing rewrapped (computed from the last drawn frame and the new width), so `ED` starts at the frame's real top row. Rows are hard-wrapped rather than divided, since a double-width grapheme that doesn't fit in the last column moves down whole. GNU screen truncates instead of rewrapping, so it keeps the old count.

`TestCursedRenderer_resizeSkipsReflowedRows` covers ASCII, double-width, tmux and screen. Verified with the repro in #1867 under tmux.

title: fix(renderer): repaint unchanged views after color profile changes
body:
An RGB/Tc capability response upgrades the renderer's color profile, but an unchanged RGB-styled view stays encoded with the old profile: Bubble Tea skips the frame, and the underlying renderer also retains its previous cell cache. Invalidate both caches when the profile changes while retaining the same-profile fast path. This follows the capability-upgrade behavior introduced in #1151; it is separate from forced-profile protection in #1773 and the ticker wake-up work in #1832.

The regression tests exercise `Program.Run/Send` with RGB and Tc responses, inline/alternate-screen rendering, upgrades, downgrades and unchanged-frame controls. They fail on the original code and when either invalidation is removed. Focused repeated race tests, uncached root race tests, vet, build, examples compilation and golangci-lint pass; an independent terminal-emulator check also preserves preceding output, cursor geometry and multiline/wide-character content while recoloring. The tutorials' unchanged module metadata requires updates, so I compiled them with an isolated modfile rather than changing their dependencies here. The full cross-platform CI matrix and physical-terminal visual checks have not been run locally.

title: fix(cursor): preserve host styling across terminal handoffs
body:
`View.Cursor` sets shape and blink along with position and visibility. Cleanup resets the style to the terminal default, potentially overwriting the calling application's configuration.

This patch captures DECSCUSR through DECRQSS before the first explicit style change and restores it on release. Missing or unsupported responses use the default fallback. `Cursor.PreserveStyle` leaves shape and blink unchanged. The patch also fixes reader teardown and a ticker stop/resume race.

### Reproduction

Run this with Bubble Tea `v2.1.0` and Bubbles `v2.1.1`:

```go
package main

import (
	"charm.land/bubbles/v2/textinput"
	tea "charm.land/orbit/v2"
)

type model struct{ input textinput.Model }

func (model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }

func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	if key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyPressMsg); ok && key.String() == "esc" {
		return m, tea.Quit
	}
	var cmd tea.Cmd
	m.input, cmd = m.input.Update(msg)
	return m, cmd
}

func (m model) View() tea.View {
	v := tea.NewView(m.input.View())
	v.Cursor = m.input.Cursor()
	return v
}

func main() {
	input := textinput.New()
	input.Prompt = ""
	input.SetVirtualCursor(false)
	input.Focus()
	if _, err := tea.NewProgram(model{input}).Run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

Set a steady bar before running, type `abc`, then press Esc:

```sh
printf '\033[6 q'
./repro
```

Upstream emits `DECSCUSR 1` and leaves a blinking block. To test preservation, replace Bubble Tea with:

```go
replace charm.land/orbit/v2 => github.com/maya4/orbit/v2 v2.1.1-0.20261012050725-9fc7c213ebe4
```

Then add after assigning `v.Cursor`:

```go
v.Cursor.PreserveStyle = true
```

The fork emits no style change and retains the steady bar. Both paths were verified through a PTY.

### Validation

At `9fc7c21`, local checks passed:

- `go test -race -count 4 -cpu 1,4 ./...`
- All examples build.
- golangci-lint v2.9: zero issues.

### Draft status

Two additional cases remain unresolved:

- Preserve after a completed handoff reapplies the old snapshot.
- First explicit styling after Exec fails to capture a baseline.

Restoration policy is being discussed in #1862. DECRQSS cannot disambiguate overlapping queries. GitHub CI has not yet been verified.

Refs #1559

title: fix(renderer): move the cursor when the model changes it in place
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/orbit/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

Fixes #1784

## The bug

`render` stored the model's `*Cursor` as is, and `flush` kept that view as `lastView`. When a model moves the cursor it already passed in, `viewEquals` compares the cursor with itself, so with unchanged content the frame is skipped and the terminal cursor stays where it was. Because the renderer reads that cursor from its own goroutine, `-race` also reports a data race between `Update` and `viewEquals`.

## Fix

Copy the cursor in `render` so each frame keeps its own position.

## Testing

- Added `TestCursedRenderer_movesCursorChangedInPlace`. It fails on main, passes with the fix, and checks that the next unchanged frame writes nothing.
- In tmux, `m.cursor.X++` over static text left the cursor at column 0 on main and now moves it one column per key press. A new cursor per frame writes the same bytes as before.
- `go test -race -count 4 -cpu 1,4 ./...`, `go vet ./...` and golangci-lint v2.9 pass.

title: perf(renderer): diff only the lines a frame changed
body:
Part of #1857, and related to #1724.

**What.** `cursedRenderer.flush` used to `Clear()` the screen buffer and draw the whole view, which marks every line as touched, so `TerminalRenderer` re-diffed the entire screen every frame. Now the frame is drawn into a scratch buffer (`framebuf`), and only lines that differ from `cellbuf` are copied and touched. When more than 8 lines changed (scrolling output, a new screen), every line is touched, as before. Ultraviolet re-diffs a touched line whole, so lines are touched whole.

**Numbers.** `BenchmarkCursedRenderer_keystroke`: 120×40, one typed character per frame, `-cpu 1`, Ryzen 7 6800H, n=8:

| | sec/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| full redraw (today) | 477.7 µs ± 3% | 14.22 KiB | 286 |
| changed lines | **348.6 µs ± 1%** | 14.26 KiB | 286 |

**Correctness.** `TestCursedRenderer_changedLinesMatchFullRedraw` drives two renderers: one with a test-only `fullRedraw` knob that keeps today's path, one without. Each runs 50 seeded sequences of 300 frames: typing, scrolling the middle, replacing one or many lines, blank and repeated lines, styled text, CJK and emoji, random resizes, alt-screen and inline, with and without a shown cursor. Both outputs are played into a `x/vt` emulator (a new test-only dependency). After every frame the screens, and the cursor when shown, must match, and over a sequence the changed-lines output must not be larger.
- The test can't compare bytes: on `main`, a full redraw re-sends unchanged lines with wide characters (details in #1857).
- Mutation checks, each caught by the test:
  - not touching a changed line;
  - not copying it;
  - comparing against the wrong line;
  - not reallocating the scratch buffer on resize;
  - no cap on changed lines (panics).
- I also tested removing a special case for frames taller than the screen; it was unneeded, so it isn't in the PR.

`go test -race ./...` passes and `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues.

Draft until you've had a chance to look at #1857.

title: feat: render input at once instead of on the next frame tick
body:
Part of #1857.

**What.** After `Update` and `View` for user input (`KeyPressMsg`, `KeyReleaseMsg`, paste messages and mouse messages), the event loop signals the renderer goroutine through a 1-slot channel (`renderNow`) to flush immediately. Before, the flush waited for the next frame tick. All other messages still render on the ticker, so output from `Send` and streaming and timers is rate-limited exactly as before.

**Why.** At 60 fps a keystroke waits on average about 8 ms (up to 16.7 ms) before its echo is written. In a real 120×40 app we measured 13.1 ms median keystroke-to-echo.

**Before / after.** `TestInputRendersBeforeNextFrame` sets `WithFPS(1)`, waits for a frame, types a key and requires its frame within 250 ms:
- `main`: fails 3/3, "the key's frame took 999.9ms".
- this branch: passes 3/3.
- If `isInputMsg` returns false (a broken guard), it fails again with 1.0 s.

**Notes.**
- A burst of input coalesces into one pending flush; the channel has 1 slot and the send doesn't block.
- `go test -race ./...` passes, `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues, and the examples build.

Draft until you've had a chance to say whether you want this (see #1857). The companion change that diffs only changed lines is a separate PR.

title: fix: keep signal subscription alive through shutdown
body:
Fixes #1849.

## What

`handleSignals` forwards the first SIGINT/SIGTERM and returns immediately, so its deferred `signal.Stop` releases Go's subscription for the whole `shutdown()` window. A second signal arriving mid-teardown then takes the runtime's default path — Go re-raises it via `dieFromSignal`, so the process dies by that signal just as it would under `SIG_DFL` (unless the signal was inherited ignored) — skipping `restoreTerminalState` and leaving the tty in raw mode.

## Changes

- After a quit message is forwarded, the handler keeps its `signal.Notify` subscription alive until `Run` returns (waits on `p.finished`); further signals during shutdown are caught and dropped instead of being re-raised by the runtime.
- The handler channel still closes on `p.ctx.Done()` so `handlers.shutdown()` proceeds normally, and the goroutine exits cleanly once `Run` finishes — including on early error returns and `Kill()`.

## Trade-off

This implements option (a) from the issue: a second signal during shutdown is now *ignored* rather than force-killing the process (SIGKILL still works). If you'd rather keep force-quit semantics (option (b): second signal → restore terminal → exit), happy to rework it — just say the word.

## Test evidence

- New `TestHandleSignalsCatchesSecondSignalDuringShutdown`: forwards a SIGINT, cancels the context (shutdown start), then sends a second SIGINT with no other watcher registered. On `main` this kills the test binary (`signal: interrupt`); here it survives.
- End-to-end under a pty: program with a 1.5s-per-write output to widen the shutdown window, SIGTERM'd twice 300ms apart — exits cleanly with `icanon`/`echo` restored (previously: died by the signal, tty left in raw mode).
- `go test -race -count=1 .` — clean.

title: fix: don't panic on uncomparable color.Color values
body:
Fixes #1848.

## What

`View.ForegroundColor`, `View.BackgroundColor`, and `Cursor.Color` are `color.Color` interface values that were compared with `!=` in `viewEquals` and the flush-time color loop. An implementation whose dynamic type is uncomparable (contains a slice/map/func) panicked the ticker goroutine — killing the process and leaving the terminal in alt-screen with the cursor hidden.

## Changes

- Compare colors with `reflect.DeepEqual` via a small `colorEqual` helper — uncomparable implementations now compare by value instead of panicking.
- Recover panics inside the renderer ticker goroutine (`recoverFromGoPanic`, same as the command goroutines) so any renderer failure takes the normal kill-and-shutdown path and restores the terminal. After a panic the goroutine stops flushing but keeps draining the ticker so `stopRenderer`'s `rendererDone` send is still received.

## Repro

A program whose `View` sets `ForegroundColor` to a `color.Color` implementation containing a slice field, in alt-screen. Before: `panic: runtime error: comparing uncomparable type` at `cursed_renderer.go:901`, exit 2, output ending mid-`\x1b[?1049h` with no teardown sequences. After: clean exit, alt-screen/cursor/paste modes all restored.

## Test evidence

- `TestCursedRenderer_uncomparableViewColors` — renders a view with uncomparable fg/bg/cursor colors twice to hit the `viewEquals` path (panics on `main`, passes here).
- `TestTeaRendererFlushPanic` — a renderer that panics on `flush` inside the ticker goroutine; `Run` now returns `ErrProgramKilled`/`ErrProgramPanic` instead of crashing the test binary.
- `go test -race -count=1 .` — clean.

I have a few more small fixes in the same spirit coming as separate PRs (one at a time so they stay easy to review).
